## Production[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

### Development[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D5&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

Paul Maslansky says he got the idea for the film when in San Francisco filming _The Right Stuff_:

> I noticed a bunch of ludicrous-looking police cadets being dressed down by a frustrated sergeant. They were an unbelievable bunch-including a lady who must have weighed over 200 pounds and a flabby man of well over 50. I asked the sergeant about them, and he explained that the mayor had ordered the department to accept a broad spectrum for the academy. "We have to take them in,"...[he said] ..."And the only thing we can do is wash them out."[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

Maslansky said he wondered "But what if they actually made it?"[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4) He took the idea to Alan Ladd Jr who agreed to finance.[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4) Neal Israel was hired to write the script with Pat Proft. Israel said:

> It's a matter of block comedy scenes. Perhaps the most recognizable was the obvious results of guys eating beans in `Blazing Saddles.' If you have four or five of these block comedy scenes in a teen-age comedy, you have a hit. If your block comedy scenes are very, very strong ones, you have a blockbuster.[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

[Dom DeLuise](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Dom_DeLuise "Dom DeLuise") was considered to direct the film but he was unavailable.[[5]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-5) Hugh Wilson was hired as director based on his success with _WKRP in Cincinnati_ even though he was not familiar with many films of this genre. He then saw a lot of those sort of movies and says "it was fairly discouraging. This immediately convinced me to cut down on the sleaze. I asked for, and got, the power to refine the Israel-Proft script. Maintaining that `funny is money,' I wanted to go for real laughter rather than going for the elements such as gratuitous sex and anti-Establishment exploits. I wanted jokes which were rooted in reality."[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

Maslansky says Wilson "took a lot of the vulgarity out; some of the very things I considered necessary. I worried that it was becoming more homogenized, and I told Hugh, `Let's keep some of the flatulence in.'"[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

Wilson says "I found out that the shower scene, the party scene and the fellatio scene were obligatory; I had to put them in. So I was stuck with trying to make those scenes as artistic as possible."[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

According to the _Los Angeles Times_, about "20 of the major elements in the movie" remain from the Israel and Proft version. Israel says that when Wilson and Maslansky turned in their rewrite to the Ladd Company, "it was rejected and the project was almost shelved. Only when they put back in dozens of our gags did the project get the go ahead."[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

Some of the scenes Wilson was unhappy with included the fellatio scene and the scene where a police sergeant was hurled into the back of a horse. A compromise was reached where these acts were not actually shown.[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

"I realize that you can carry grossness, rudeness and crudeness just so far before the audience finds it terribly repetitive and not so funny," said Wilson. "After the enormous success of _Police Academy_, I no longer believe that you have to show the female breast or make cruel ethnic jokes-not to mention the rampant sexism. And you don't have to reproduce the sounds that an overfed body makes."[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

### Filming[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D6&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

Opening scenes were shot in Toronto, Ontario. The camera booth scene was shot on the Cherry Street Bridge in Toronto.[[6]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-6) The Academy itself was previously the site of the Lakeshore Psychiatric Hospital in Etobicoke, and has since become the Lakeshore campus of Humber College.[[7]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-7) The studio scenes were shot at Lakeshore Film Studios; the city scenes were filmed in various parts of Toronto.[[8]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-8) The riot scenes was filmed at Kensington Market in Toronto, The Silver Dollar Bar at Spadina Avenue is the real name of the bar were was filmed for the _Blue Oyster Bar_ scenes.

## Reception[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D10&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

### Box office[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D11&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

_Police Academy_ opened in the number 1 spot in 1,587 U.S. theaters on March 23, 1984, to a first weekend total gross of $8.6 million. The film went on to gross $81.2 million, becoming the 6th highest grossing American film of 1984.[[11]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-mojo-11) It grossed $68.6 million overseas for a total worldwide gross of $149.8 million.[[12]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-block-12) The film made a profit of $35 million.[[12]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-block-12)

### Critical response[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D12&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

The film received mixed reviews from critics.[[13]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-13) On Rotten Tomatoes the film has an approval rating of 55% based on 29 reviews. The critical consensus reads, "_Police Academy_ is rude, crude, and proudly sophomoric -- which is either a condemnation or a ringing endorsement, depending on your taste in comedy."[[14]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-14) On Metacritic the film has a score of 41 out of 100 based on reviews from 6 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews".[[15]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-15)

Roger Ebert of the _Chicago Sun-Times_, gave the film zero stars out of four, commenting that "It's really something. It's so bad, maybe you should pool your money and draw straws and send one of the guys off to rent it so that in the future, whenever you think you're sitting through a bad comedy, he could shake his head, and chuckle tolerantly, and explain that you don't know what bad is".[[16]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-16) Ebert's zero-stars review of the film became famous because (unlike many other films he gave zero star ratings to, including I Spit On Your Grave and Freddy Got Fingered), he did not state that "Police Academy" was diseased or morally deficient: he simply found it to be a comedy nadir that not only had no laughs, but didn't seem to be trying to make people laugh.

Critic Vincent Canby of _The New York Times_, gave the film a mixed review, saying "The movie plows through one outrageous sequence to the next with the momentum of a freight train".[[17]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-17) Rita Kemply of the Washington Post wrote: "Attention all units: Slapstick in progress in the vicinity of Police Academy. Suspects wanted for mugging the camera and possession of night shtiks with intent to incite a laugh riot. Please respond to this blues burlesque, a uniformly funny hit sure to have a long run. Its target audience -- those who can take their T&A with a grain of assault. Its plot -- a combo of _Animal House_ and _An Officer and a Gentleman_. Its stars -- a rainbow coalition of hot newcomers and dependable, unexpendable pros."[[18]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-18)

Producer Paul Maslansky says that original feedback on the film was that it was not gross enough. "What are you trying to do?, make a damned _Tootsie_?" said one executive. "Paul, it doesn't fit the formula; it needs more flatulence, more slobbishness, more T&A.," said another.[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

_**Police Academy**_ is a 1984 American comedy film directed by Hugh Wilson in his directorial debut, and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures. Its story follows a new recruitment policy for an unnamed police department's academy that is required to take in any recruit who wishes to try out to be a police officer. The film stars Steve Guttenberg, Kim Cattrall, and G.W. Bailey.

The film was produced by The Ladd Company. It premiered on March 23, 1984. It grossed $8.5 million in its opening weekend and over $149 million worldwide, against a budget of $4.5 million, and remains the most successful film of the series as of 2022. The film spawned six sequels in the Police Academy franchise.

## Plot[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

Due to a shortage of police officers, Mary Sue Beal, the mayor of an unnamed city, requires the police department to accept all recruits. Easy-going Carey Mahoney, who has repeatedly gotten in legal trouble while standing up to arrogance, is given a choice by Police Captain Reed: enroll in the police academy or go to jail. Mahoney agrees to the former, but plans to be such a bad student that he's expelled. The chief of police, Henry Hurst, outraged by the Mayor's plan, decides to make the experience so bad for the new recruits that they give up.

Lieutenant Thaddeus Harris makes their lives miserable, though Commandant Eric Lassard wants to give the new cadets a chance. Harris appoints Copeland and Blankes as squad leaders to help him.

Lassard reveals to Mahoney his deal with Capt. Reed to keep him at the police academy for the full term. Mahoney falls in love with cadet Karen Thompson and befriends fellow cadets Larvell Jones, a human beatbox, ladies' man George Martin, gun-obsessed security guard Eugene Tackleberry, cowardly man Leslie Barbara, accident-prone Douglas Fackler and gentle giant Moses Hightower.

Blankes and Copeland investigate a party organized by Mahoney, who tricks them by saying that the party is at the Blue Oyster, a gay bar. The pair plant a prostitute in Mahoney's dormitory, to be found during room checks. While smuggling her off the campus, Mahoney is forced to hide with her under a lectern as Commandant Lassard leads in a group of officers. While Mahoney is not looking, the prostitute performs fellatio on Lassard. Mahoney steps out from under the lectern but finds Lassard still present, leading Lassard to assume Mahoney did it.

Hightower reveals to Mahoney that he has not driven a car since he was 12. To help Hightower prepare for a driving test, they steal Copeland's car. After Hightower passes the test, Copeland racially insults cadet Laverne Hooks for an accident. Hightower, angered by the insult, overturns the car with Copeland inside. Harris ejects Hightower from the academy, upsetting the other cadets.

Blankes and Copeland fail to trick Mahoney into fighting them after they find Copeland's destroyed car. Barbara stands up for Mahoney and knocks Copeland out with a lunch tray. Blankes retaliates, and Mahoney becomes involved in a brawl. When Harris asks who started the fight, Mahoney takes the blame to protect Barbara's standing and is expelled.

While downtown, Fackler throws an apple out of a police car, which hits a man on the back of the head; this triggers a chain reaction of violence which quickly escalates into a general riot. Mahoney, just about to leave, instead joins the other cadets to pacify the crowd. The cadets are accidentally transported to the epicenter of the rioting, and one criminal steals Blankes and Copeland's revolvers, whereupon the two hide out in the Blue Oyster Bar. A rioter gang captures Harris, with their group leader taking him as a hostage. Mahoney attempts to rescue Harris but is also taken hostage. Hightower appears, deceives the madman, and knocks him down a set of stairs, to be arrested by Hooks.

Mahoney and Hightower are both reinstated, and for rescuing Harris and capturing his kidnapper, they receive the academy's highest commendation and medals. The film ends with all cadets graduating.

## Production[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

### Development[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D5&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

Paul Maslansky says he got the idea for the film when in San Francisco filming _The Right Stuff_:

> I noticed a bunch of ludicrous-looking police cadets being dressed down by a frustrated sergeant. They were an unbelievable bunch-including a lady who must have weighed over 200 pounds and a flabby man of well over 50. I asked the sergeant about them, and he explained that the mayor had ordered the department to accept a broad spectrum for the academy. "We have to take them in,"...[he said] ..."And the only thing we can do is wash them out."[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

Maslansky said he wondered "But what if they actually made it?"[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4) He took the idea to Alan Ladd Jr who agreed to finance.[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4) Neal Israel was hired to write the script with Pat Proft. Israel said:

> It's a matter of block comedy scenes. Perhaps the most recognizable was the obvious results of guys eating beans in `Blazing Saddles.' If you have four or five of these block comedy scenes in a teen-age comedy, you have a hit. If your block comedy scenes are very, very strong ones, you have a blockbuster.[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

[Dom DeLuise](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Dom_DeLuise "Dom DeLuise") was considered to direct the film but he was unavailable.[[5]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-5) Hugh Wilson was hired as director based on his success with _WKRP in Cincinnati_ even though he was not familiar with many films of this genre. He then saw a lot of those sort of movies and says "it was fairly discouraging. This immediately convinced me to cut down on the sleaze. I asked for, and got, the power to refine the Israel-Proft script. Maintaining that `funny is money,' I wanted to go for real laughter rather than going for the elements such as gratuitous sex and anti-Establishment exploits. I wanted jokes which were rooted in reality."[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

Maslansky says Wilson "took a lot of the vulgarity out; some of the very things I considered necessary. I worried that it was becoming more homogenized, and I told Hugh, `Let's keep some of the flatulence in.'"[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

Wilson says "I found out that the shower scene, the party scene and the fellatio scene were obligatory; I had to put them in. So I was stuck with trying to make those scenes as artistic as possible."[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

According to the _Los Angeles Times_, about "20 of the major elements in the movie" remain from the Israel and Proft version. Israel says that when Wilson and Maslansky turned in their rewrite to the Ladd Company, "it was rejected and the project was almost shelved. Only when they put back in dozens of our gags did the project get the go ahead."[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

Some of the scenes Wilson was unhappy with included the fellatio scene and the scene where a police sergeant was hurled into the back of a horse. A compromise was reached where these acts were not actually shown.[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

"I realize that you can carry grossness, rudeness and crudeness just so far before the audience finds it terribly repetitive and not so funny," said Wilson. "After the enormous success of _Police Academy_, I no longer believe that you have to show the female breast or make cruel ethnic jokes-not to mention the rampant sexism. And you don't have to reproduce the sounds that an overfed body makes."[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

### Filming[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D6&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

Opening scenes were shot in Toronto, Ontario. The camera booth scene was shot on the Cherry Street Bridge in Toronto.[[6]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-6) The Academy itself was previously the site of the Lakeshore Psychiatric Hospital in Etobicoke, and has since become the Lakeshore campus of Humber College.[[7]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-7) The studio scenes were shot at Lakeshore Film Studios; the city scenes were filmed in various parts of Toronto.[[8]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-8) The riot scenes was filmed at Kensington Market in Toronto, The Silver Dollar Bar at Spadina Avenue is the real name of the bar were was filmed for the _Blue Oyster Bar_ scenes.

This set contains the first four films in the series on three discs: the first two films separately, and the third and fourth films on one double-sided disc. Police Academy 5-7 would be released in a DVD set entitled "4 Film Favorites: Cop Comedy Collection", packaged with _Loaded Weapon 1_.
*   _Police Academy: What an Institution!_ Blu-ray was released 1 July 2013 as a Region Free Blu-ray. This Blu-ray contains one disc and special features.[[10]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-10)

## Reception[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D10&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

### Box office[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D11&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

_Police Academy_ opened in the number 1 spot in 1,587 U.S. theaters on March 23, 1984, to a first weekend total gross of $8.6 million. The film went on to gross $81.2 million, becoming the 6th highest grossing American film of 1984.[[11]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-mojo-11) It grossed $68.6 million overseas for a total worldwide gross of $149.8 million.[[12]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-block-12) The film made a profit of $35 million.[[12]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-block-12)

### Critical response[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwarnerbros.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FPolice_Academy_%28film%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D12&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

The film received mixed reviews from critics.[[13]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-13) On Rotten Tomatoes the film has an approval rating of 55% based on 29 reviews. The critical consensus reads, "_Police Academy_ is rude, crude, and proudly sophomoric -- which is either a condemnation or a ringing endorsement, depending on your taste in comedy."[[14]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-14) On Metacritic the film has a score of 41 out of 100 based on reviews from 6 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews".[[15]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-15)

Roger Ebert of the _Chicago Sun-Times_, gave the film zero stars out of four, commenting that "It's really something. It's so bad, maybe you should pool your money and draw straws and send one of the guys off to rent it so that in the future, whenever you think you're sitting through a bad comedy, he could shake his head, and chuckle tolerantly, and explain that you don't know what bad is".[[16]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-16) Ebert's zero-stars review of the film became famous because (unlike many other films he gave zero star ratings to, including I Spit On Your Grave and Freddy Got Fingered), he did not state that "Police Academy" was diseased or morally deficient: he simply found it to be a comedy nadir that not only had no laughs, but didn't seem to be trying to make people laugh.

Critic Vincent Canby of _The New York Times_, gave the film a mixed review, saying "The movie plows through one outrageous sequence to the next with the momentum of a freight train".[[17]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-17) Rita Kemply of the Washington Post wrote: "Attention all units: Slapstick in progress in the vicinity of Police Academy. Suspects wanted for mugging the camera and possession of night shtiks with intent to incite a laugh riot. Please respond to this blues burlesque, a uniformly funny hit sure to have a long run. Its target audience -- those who can take their T&A with a grain of assault. Its plot -- a combo of _Animal House_ and _An Officer and a Gentleman_. Its stars -- a rainbow coalition of hot newcomers and dependable, unexpendable pros."[[18]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-18)

Producer Paul Maslansky says that original feedback on the film was that it was not gross enough. "What are you trying to do?, make a damned _Tootsie_?" said one executive. "Paul, it doesn't fit the formula; it needs more flatulence, more slobbishness, more T&A.," said another.[[4]](https://warnerbros.fandom.com/wiki/Police_Academy_(film)#cite_note-latimes-4)

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

_**Police Academy**_ is an American [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film") franchise of seven [theatrical films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movie_theater "Movie theater") and two [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin-off_media "Spin-off media")[television shows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_program "Television program"). The 1984 film _[Police Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police\_Academy\_(film) "Police Academy (film)")_ followed the premise of a new mayor requiring the local police department to accept all recruits. The film franchise relies heavily on [slapstick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slapstick "Slapstick") humor and [physical comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_comedy "Physical comedy"), as the misfit recruits attempt to prove themselves capable of being police officers, succeeding despite their eccentricities. The first four films follow Carey Mahoney ([Steve Guttenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Guttenberg "Steve Guttenberg")), a repeat offender forced to join the [police academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academy "Police academy") as punishment. The 1994 film _[Mission to Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police\_Academy:\_Mission\_to\_Moscow "Police Academy: Mission to Moscow")_ marked the seventh installment, with cast members [George Gaynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Gaynes "George Gaynes"), [Michael Winslow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Winslow "Michael Winslow"), and [David Graf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Graf "David Graf") appearing throughout the film series.

The first film grossed $149.8 million worldwide.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-block-1) While the subsequent films failed to impress critics, they sustained commercial success, grossing $391 million in total.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-block-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-pa7-2) Parallels have been drawn between _Police Academy_ and the British _[Carry On](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carry\_On\_(franchise) "Carry On (franchise)")_ series,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-3) for their common tropes of a returning ensemble cast, frequent use of [lowbrow humor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_comedy "Low comedy"), and reliance on sexual innuendo.

Guttenberg announced in September 2018 that a new _Police Academy_ movie was in the works after spending years in [development hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Development_hell "Development hell").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-police-academy-8-4)

### _Police Academy_ (1984)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Police Academy (1984)")]

Main article: [Police Academy (film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(film) "Police Academy (film)")

_Police Academy_ was released in 1984 and directed by [Hugh Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Wilson_(director) "Hugh Wilson (director)"). The film has a newly elected female mayor announcing a policy requiring the police department to accept all willing recruits. The movie followed a group of misfit recruits in their attempts to prove themselves capable of being police officers and their adventures at the police academy.

### _Police Academy 2: Their First Assignment_ (1985)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Police Academy 2: Their First Assignment (1985)")]

Main article: [Police Academy 2: Their First Assignment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_2:_Their_First_Assignment "Police Academy 2: Their First Assignment")

In _Police Academy 2: Their First Assignment_, the newly graduated cadets are sent to one of the worst [precincts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_precinct "Police precinct") in the city to improve the conditions. Lt. Mauser undermines their attempts so he can get Capt. Lassard fired and get the position in charge.

### _Police Academy 3: Back in Training_ (1986)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Police Academy 3: Back in Training (1986)")]

Main article: [Police Academy 3: Back in Training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_3:_Back_in_Training "Police Academy 3: Back in Training")

_Police Academy 3: Back in Training_ was released in 1986, and like its predecessor, was directed by [Jerry Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Paris "Jerry Paris"). When the governor of the state announces that budget cuts necessitate the closure of the worst of the two police academies, the officers of the Metropolitan Police Academy, led by Commandant Lassard, work on ensuring it is not theirs. This is hindered by their unusual gang of new cadets.

### _Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol_ (1987)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol (1987)")]

Main article: [Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_4:_Citizens_on_Patrol "Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol")

_Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol_, released in 1987 and directed by [Jim Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Drake_(director) "Jim Drake (director)"), involves new recruits being brought in when the officers work with a newly formed Citizens on Patrol group. Harris and Proctor are in charge, though, and plan to dismantle the program. _Citizens on Patrol_ was the final film starring Guttenberg.

### _Police Academy 5: Assignment Miami Beach_ (1988)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Police Academy 5: Assignment Miami Beach (1988)")]

Main article: [Police Academy 5: Assignment Miami Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_5:_Assignment_Miami_Beach "Police Academy 5: Assignment Miami Beach")

_Police Academy 5: Assignment Miami Beach_, released in 1988, was directed by [Alan Myerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Myerson "Alan Myerson"). The plot involves the officers attending a police convention in [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida") to honor Commandant Eric Lassard as [police officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_officer "Police officer") of the decade, wherein he inadvertently switches his sports bag with that of a group of jewel thieves. The thieves try to get it back.

### _Police Academy 6: City Under Siege_ (1989)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Police Academy 6: City Under Siege (1989)")]

Main article: [Police Academy 6: City Under Siege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_6:_City_Under_Siege "Police Academy 6: City Under Siege")

The sixth installment, _Police Academy 6: City Under Siege_, directed by [Peter Bonerz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bonerz "Peter Bonerz"), was released in 1989. When the city suffers from a dangerous set of crimes by a gang of jewel thieves, the Metropolitan Police Academy graduates are brought in to do something about it.

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Police Academy: Mission to Moscow (1994)")]

_Police Academy: Mission to Moscow_, released in 1994 and directed by Alan Metter, involved the officers going to [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") to help catch an international crime figure.

### Future

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Future")]

A franchise reboot has been in various stages of [development hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Development_hell "Development hell") since September 2003,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-police-academy-8-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-Police_Academy_8_is_in_the_works-5) when the eighth _Police Academy_ film was announced with a tentative release scheduled for 2007. The studio acknowledged the franchise's return after more than thirteen years of absence,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-Police_Academy_8_is_in_the_works-5) Paul Maslansky stated, "I felt it was time to start again. I saw that _[Starsky & Hutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starsky\_&\_Hutch\_(film) "Starsky & Hutch (film)")_ and a number of other revivals were doing really well. _Police Academy_ has such a great history, so I thought, 'Why not?'"[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-6) with most of the main cast members set to return.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-7) Hugh Wilson was later slated to direct.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-8)[Leslie Easterbrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leslie_Easterbrook "Leslie Easterbrook") (Capt. Debbie Callahan) and [Marion Ramsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_Ramsey "Marion Ramsey") (Sgt. Laverne Hooks) mentioned that filming for the next _Police Academy_ film was scheduled to commence principal photography mid-2006 to meet its 2007 release.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-9) The film was suspended in October 2006, at which point Easterbrook mentioned that the project may be repurposed as a direct-to-DVD sequel. She added that though [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Entertainment "Warner Bros. Entertainment") wanted to do a new film, they wanted a producer to get independent financing.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-11)

In May 2008, Michael Winslow replied to a question about a possible new _Police Academy_ film: "Anything's possible. You've got to hope for Paul Maslansky and those folks over there to put it together. It's up to them. It would be great to see everyone again."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-12) In November of the same year, Steve Guttenberg (Sgt. Carey Mahoney) confirmed that _8_ was still in development and that he was working on the script with Warner Bros.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-13)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] Guttenberg is slated to direct the film,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-Moviehole-14) and stated that all living cast members from the previous installments would return to reprise their roles.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-Moviehole-14)

In March 2010, New Line announced plans to revive the _Police Academy_ franchise, with a new film in development with Paul Maslansky attached as filmmaker. Maslansky stated, "It's going to be very worthwhile to the people who remember it and to those who saw it on TV ... It's going to be a new class. We hope to discover new talent and season it with great comedians. It'll be anything but another movie with a numeral next to it. And we'll most probably retain the wonderful musical theme."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-15) Later that month, the filmmaker stated that he plans to bring back some of the original cast to train the new recruits.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-16) While appearing as a guest on the July 12, 2010, edition of _[This Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Morning\_(TV\_series) "This Morning (TV series)")_, Michael Winslow (Sgt. Larvell Jones) confirmed that _Police Academy 8_ was in active development. In August 2010, Steve Guttenberg revealed a script was being written by [David Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Diamond_(screenwriter) "David Diamond (screenwriter)") and [David Weissman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Weissman "David Weissman").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-interview-17) In August 2010, actor [Bobcat Goldthwait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobcat_Goldthwait "Bobcat Goldthwait") (Officer Zed) released a statement urging Hollywood to reboot the _Police Academy_ series with a new group of actors instead of the original cast members. Goldthwait confirmed that Steve Guttenberg would return and that movie bosses were trying to get [Kim Cattrall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Cattrall "Kim Cattrall") and [Sharon Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharon_Stone "Sharon Stone") to return for an eighth film, though Goldthwait said he had no desire to return to the series.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-18)

By January 2012, [New Line Cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Line_Cinema "New Line Cinema") announced that Scott Zabielski would replace Maslansky as the director of the upcoming film.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-19) Later in March of the same year, [Michael Winslow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Winslow "Michael Winslow") stated that production of the eighth film tentatively scheduled to commence that November, and that an offer had been made to [Shaquille O'Neal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaquille_O'Neal "Shaquille O'Neal") to replace the late [Bubba Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubba_Smith "Bubba Smith") as Hightower.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-20) In June 2012, [Jeremy Garelick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Garelick "Jeremy Garelick") was hired to contribute to a rewrite the aforementioned script.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-22) In April 2014, [Keegan-Michael Key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keegan-Michael_Key "Keegan-Michael Key") and [Jordan Peele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Peele "Jordan Peele"), from the sketch show _[Key & Peele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key\_&\_Peele "Key & Peele")_ were brought in produce the film.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-23) Steve Guttenberg shared his excitement with the project in July 2015, as the project was rumored to be titled _Police Academy: Next Generation._[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-24) In April 2016, the two said that the project was still ongoing and that it was going to be influenced by _[End of Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End\_of\_Watch "End of Watch")_ and [_M*A*S*H_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M*A*S*H_(TV_series) "M*A*S*H (TV series)"). They said that the project would be a "funny take on a grounded, real approach as the Key and Peele way", and noted that it would give them access to talk about what was going on in the landscape at the time.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-26) After years of delays, Steve Guttenberg announced in September 2018, that the sequel was once again in active development; stating, "the next _Police Academy_ is coming, no details yet, but it is in a gift bag being readied!"[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-27) In 2021, when asked about an eight film, Guttenberg replied with "I suspect you haven't seen the last of my Mahoney".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-28) In 2026, it was revealed that Key and Peele's reboot had been scrapped in 2014 following the [death of Michael Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_Michael_Brown "Killing of Michael Brown"), as the studio felt it would be in poor taste to release a comedy film about police officers.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-29)

_**Police Academy**_ is an American [comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_film "Comedy film") franchise of seven [theatrical films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movie_theater "Movie theater") and two [spin-off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin-off_media "Spin-off media")[television shows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_program "Television program"). The 1984 film _[Police Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police\_Academy\_(film) "Police Academy (film)")_ followed the premise of a new mayor requiring the local police department to accept all recruits. The film franchise relies heavily on [slapstick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slapstick "Slapstick") humor and [physical comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_comedy "Physical comedy"), as the misfit recruits attempt to prove themselves capable of being police officers, succeeding despite their eccentricities. The first four films follow Carey Mahoney ([Steve Guttenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Guttenberg "Steve Guttenberg")), a repeat offender forced to join the [police academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academy "Police academy") as punishment. The 1994 film _[Mission to Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police\_Academy:\_Mission\_to\_Moscow "Police Academy: Mission to Moscow")_ marked the seventh installment, with cast members [George Gaynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Gaynes "George Gaynes"), [Michael Winslow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Winslow "Michael Winslow"), and [David Graf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Graf "David Graf") appearing throughout the film series.

The first film grossed $149.8 million worldwide.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-block-1) While the subsequent films failed to impress critics, they sustained commercial success, grossing $391 million in total.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-block-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-pa7-2) Parallels have been drawn between _Police Academy_ and the British _[Carry On](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carry\_On\_(franchise) "Carry On (franchise)")_ series,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-3) for their common tropes of a returning ensemble cast, frequent use of [lowbrow humor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_comedy "Low comedy"), and reliance on sexual innuendo.

Guttenberg announced in September 2018 that a new _Police Academy_ movie was in the works after spending years in [development hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Development_hell "Development hell").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-police-academy-8-4)

### _Police Academy_ (1984)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Police Academy (1984)")]

Main article: [Police Academy (film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(film) "Police Academy (film)")

_Police Academy_ was released in 1984 and directed by [Hugh Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Wilson_(director) "Hugh Wilson (director)"). The film has a newly elected female mayor announcing a policy requiring the police department to accept all willing recruits. The movie followed a group of misfit recruits in their attempts to prove themselves capable of being police officers and their adventures at the police academy.

### _Police Academy 2: Their First Assignment_ (1985)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Police Academy 2: Their First Assignment (1985)")]

Main article: [Police Academy 2: Their First Assignment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_2:_Their_First_Assignment "Police Academy 2: Their First Assignment")

In _Police Academy 2: Their First Assignment_, the newly graduated cadets are sent to one of the worst [precincts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_precinct "Police precinct") in the city to improve the conditions. Lt. Mauser undermines their attempts so he can get Capt. Lassard fired and get the position in charge.

### _Police Academy 3: Back in Training_ (1986)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Police Academy 3: Back in Training (1986)")]

Main article: [Police Academy 3: Back in Training](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_3:_Back_in_Training "Police Academy 3: Back in Training")

_Police Academy 3: Back in Training_ was released in 1986, and like its predecessor, was directed by [Jerry Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Paris "Jerry Paris"). When the governor of the state announces that budget cuts necessitate the closure of the worst of the two police academies, the officers of the Metropolitan Police Academy, led by Commandant Lassard, work on ensuring it is not theirs. This is hindered by their unusual gang of new cadets.

### _Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol_ (1987)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol (1987)")]

Main article: [Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_4:_Citizens_on_Patrol "Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol")

_Police Academy 4: Citizens on Patrol_, released in 1987 and directed by [Jim Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Drake_(director) "Jim Drake (director)"), involves new recruits being brought in when the officers work with a newly formed Citizens on Patrol group. Harris and Proctor are in charge, though, and plan to dismantle the program. _Citizens on Patrol_ was the final film starring Guttenberg.

### _Police Academy 5: Assignment Miami Beach_ (1988)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Police Academy 5: Assignment Miami Beach (1988)")]

Main article: [Police Academy 5: Assignment Miami Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_5:_Assignment_Miami_Beach "Police Academy 5: Assignment Miami Beach")

_Police Academy 5: Assignment Miami Beach_, released in 1988, was directed by [Alan Myerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Myerson "Alan Myerson"). The plot involves the officers attending a police convention in [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida") to honor Commandant Eric Lassard as [police officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_officer "Police officer") of the decade, wherein he inadvertently switches his sports bag with that of a group of jewel thieves. The thieves try to get it back.

### _Police Academy 6: City Under Siege_ (1989)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Police Academy 6: City Under Siege (1989)")]

Main article: [Police Academy 6: City Under Siege](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_6:_City_Under_Siege "Police Academy 6: City Under Siege")

The sixth installment, _Police Academy 6: City Under Siege_, directed by [Peter Bonerz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bonerz "Peter Bonerz"), was released in 1989. When the city suffers from a dangerous set of crimes by a gang of jewel thieves, the Metropolitan Police Academy graduates are brought in to do something about it.

### _Police Academy: Mission to Moscow_ (1994)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Police Academy: Mission to Moscow (1994)")]

Main article: [Police Academy: Mission to Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy:_Mission_to_Moscow "Police Academy: Mission to Moscow")

_Police Academy: Mission to Moscow_, released in 1994 and directed by Alan Metter, involved the officers going to [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia") to help catch an international crime figure.

### Future

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_Academy_(franchise)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Future")]

A franchise reboot has been in various stages of [development hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Development_hell "Development hell") since September 2003,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-police-academy-8-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-Police_Academy_8_is_in_the_works-5) when the eighth _Police Academy_ film was announced with a tentative release scheduled for 2007. The studio acknowledged the franchise's return after more than thirteen years of absence,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-Police_Academy_8_is_in_the_works-5) Paul Maslansky stated, "I felt it was time to start again. I saw that _[Starsky & Hutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starsky\_&\_Hutch\_(film) "Starsky & Hutch (film)")_ and a number of other revivals were doing really well. _Police Academy_ has such a great history, so I thought, 'Why not?'"[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-6) with most of the main cast members set to return.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-7) Hugh Wilson was later slated to direct.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-8)[Leslie Easterbrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leslie_Easterbrook "Leslie Easterbrook") (Capt. Debbie Callahan) and [Marion Ramsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_Ramsey "Marion Ramsey") (Sgt. Laverne Hooks) mentioned that filming for the next _Police Academy_ film was scheduled to commence principal photography mid-2006 to meet its 2007 release.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-9) The film was suspended in October 2006, at which point Easterbrook mentioned that the project may be repurposed as a direct-to-DVD sequel. She added that though [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros._Entertainment "Warner Bros. Entertainment") wanted to do a new film, they wanted a producer to get independent financing.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-11)

In May 2008, Michael Winslow replied to a question about a possible new _Police Academy_ film: "Anything's possible. You've got to hope for Paul Maslansky and those folks over there to put it together. It's up to them. It would be great to see everyone again."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-12) In November of the same year, Steve Guttenberg (Sgt. Carey Mahoney) confirmed that _8_ was still in development and that he was working on the script with Warner Bros.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-13)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] Guttenberg is slated to direct the film,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-Moviehole-14) and stated that all living cast members from the previous installments would return to reprise their roles.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-Moviehole-14)

In March 2010, New Line announced plans to revive the _Police Academy_ franchise, with a new film in development with Paul Maslansky attached as filmmaker. Maslansky stated, "It's going to be very worthwhile to the people who remember it and to those who saw it on TV ... It's going to be a new class. We hope to discover new talent and season it with great comedians. It'll be anything but another movie with a numeral next to it. And we'll most probably retain the wonderful musical theme."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-15) Later that month, the filmmaker stated that he plans to bring back some of the original cast to train the new recruits.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-16) While appearing as a guest on the July 12, 2010, edition of _[This Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Morning\_(TV\_series) "This Morning (TV series)")_, Michael Winslow (Sgt. Larvell Jones) confirmed that _Police Academy 8_ was in active development. In August 2010, Steve Guttenberg revealed a script was being written by [David Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Diamond_(screenwriter) "David Diamond (screenwriter)") and [David Weissman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Weissman "David Weissman").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-interview-17) In August 2010, actor [Bobcat Goldthwait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobcat_Goldthwait "Bobcat Goldthwait") (Officer Zed) released a statement urging Hollywood to reboot the _Police Academy_ series with a new group of actors instead of the original cast members. Goldthwait confirmed that Steve Guttenberg would return and that movie bosses were trying to get [Kim Cattrall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Cattrall "Kim Cattrall") and [Sharon Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharon_Stone "Sharon Stone") to return for an eighth film, though Goldthwait said he had no desire to return to the series.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-18)

By January 2012, [New Line Cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Line_Cinema "New Line Cinema") announced that Scott Zabielski would replace Maslansky as the director of the upcoming film.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-19) Later in March of the same year, [Michael Winslow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Winslow "Michael Winslow") stated that production of the eighth film tentatively scheduled to commence that November, and that an offer had been made to [Shaquille O'Neal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaquille_O'Neal "Shaquille O'Neal") to replace the late [Bubba Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubba_Smith "Bubba Smith") as Hightower.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-20) In June 2012, [Jeremy Garelick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Garelick "Jeremy Garelick") was hired to contribute to a rewrite the aforementioned script.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-22) In April 2014, [Keegan-Michael Key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keegan-Michael_Key "Keegan-Michael Key") and [Jordan Peele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Peele "Jordan Peele"), from the sketch show _[Key & Peele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key\_&\_Peele "Key & Peele")_ were brought in produce the film.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-23) Steve Guttenberg shared his excitement with the project in July 2015, as the project was rumored to be titled _Police Academy: Next Generation._[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-24) In April 2016, the two said that the project was still ongoing and that it was going to be influenced by _[End of Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End\_of\_Watch "End of Watch")_ and [_M*A*S*H_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M*A*S*H_(TV_series) "M*A*S*H (TV series)"). They said that the project would be a "funny take on a grounded, real approach as the Key and Peele way", and noted that it would give them access to talk about what was going on in the landscape at the time.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-26) After years of delays, Steve Guttenberg announced in September 2018, that the sequel was once again in active development; stating, "the next _Police Academy_ is coming, no details yet, but it is in a gift bag being readied!"[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-27) In 2021, when asked about an eight film, Guttenberg replied with "I suspect you haven't seen the last of my Mahoney".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-28) In 2026, it was revealed that Key and Peele's reboot had been scrapped in 2014 following the [death of Michael Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_Michael_Brown "Killing of Michael Brown"), as the studio felt it would be in poor taste to release a comedy film about police officers.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Academy_(franchise)#cite_note-29)

PUBLISHED 7:00 AM CT May 03, 2025 PUBLISHED 7:00 AM CDT May 03, 2025

SHARE

O’FALLON, Mo.—St. Charles City and O’Fallon police chiefs and mayors joined other local leaders to cut the ribbon for the completion of phase one of the Center for Advanced Skills Training and Law Enforcement (CASTLE).

* * *

#### **What You Need To Know**

##### *   Saint Charles County-based leaders and police cut the ribbon for the phase one completion of the Center for Advanced Skills Training and Law Enforcement or CASTLE
  
*   With the firing range finished, phase 2’s construction starts soon

*   Phase two includes an expansion to phase one’s firing range, a one-mile emergency vehicle operations course, a two-story simunition house, a canine obstacle course training area, a SWAT training area that includes a school bus and fuselage, a drone training area and a training center
  
*   Eastern Missouri Police Academy will move to CASTLE upon phase twos planned completion by late 2026

* * *

“Just last June, less than a year ago, we were here to break ground on this monumental endeavor,” said O'Fallon, Mo. Mayor Bill Hennessey. “What we’re accomplishing here will benefit everyone for generations to come."  
  
 He added, "Since the groundbreaking, both cities have created a governing board that will manage the day-to-day construction activities and will ensure the training offered here is top-notch.”

“My gratitude to you all,” said Mayor Dan Borgmeyer, St. Charles. “Nothing makes me prouder than the mayor of St. Charles than to say, we’re safe. This is going to be an amazing project.”

With the firing range finished, the second phase of construction will start soon with completion in late 2026. Phase two includes an expansion to phase one’s firing range, a one-mile emergency vehicle operations course, a two-story simunition house, a canine obstacle course training area, a SWAT training area that includes a school bus and fuselage, a drone training area and a training center. That center will house seven classrooms and a virtual training room.

“Currently, there’s not a facility comprised of all these areas in this region,” said Josh Hoeing, Captain for St. Charles City Police Department. “We hope to provide the highest quality of law enforcement training to not only our neighboring municipalities but the entire Midwest region and the country. This center will be a one-stop shop for departments to send their officers.”

Eastern Missouri Police Academy (EMPA) will rehome to CASTLE upon phase two’s completion. The Academy’s board approved the rehoming weeks ago but had to wait for its attorney to sign off on it before they were able to put pen to paper on May 1.

“We really have nice facilities,” said Dr. Thomas Leasor, Executive Director for Eastern Missouri Police Academy. “But as far as the extra type of training—it’s scattered _.”_

EMPA is currently located in Lake St. Louis but attendees have to travel throughout the county for various training functions.

“This will be such a tremendous opportunity to for us to get everything in one location. Our recruits will be around cops every single day. We do a lot of continued education as well but just the facilities and the cooperative group coming together is just such a tremendous opportunity for the academy.”

Leasor noted that training is often brought into question in a courtroom and he commends everyone involved for the CASTLE project.

“It is so profound that these agencies have recognized, and their communities have recognized the demand for training and how that equates to better officers out on the street being able to interact with the public, being able to be trained to use the technology that’s here today.”

NEWS

# First phase of new St. Charles County police training facility open

BY  John Gerding St. Louis

PUBLISHED 7:00 AM CT May 03, 2025 PUBLISHED 7:00 AM CDT May 03, 2025

SHARE

O’FALLON, Mo.—St. Charles City and O’Fallon police chiefs and mayors joined other local leaders to cut the ribbon for the completion of phase one of the Center for Advanced Skills Training and Law Enforcement (CASTLE).

* * *

#### **What You Need To Know**

##### *   Saint Charles County-based leaders and police cut the ribbon for the phase one completion of the Center for Advanced Skills Training and Law Enforcement or CASTLE
  
*   With the firing range finished, phase 2’s construction starts soon

*   Phase two includes an expansion to phase one’s firing range, a one-mile emergency vehicle operations course, a two-story simunition house, a canine obstacle course training area, a SWAT training area that includes a school bus and fuselage, a drone training area and a training center
  
*   Eastern Missouri Police Academy will move to CASTLE upon phase twos planned completion by late 2026

* * *

“Just last June, less than a year ago, we were here to break ground on this monumental endeavor,” said O'Fallon, Mo. Mayor Bill Hennessey. “What we’re accomplishing here will benefit everyone for generations to come."  
  
 He added, "Since the groundbreaking, both cities have created a governing board that will manage the day-to-day construction activities and will ensure the training offered here is top-notch.”

“My gratitude to you all,” said Mayor Dan Borgmeyer, St. Charles. “Nothing makes me prouder than the mayor of St. Charles than to say, we’re safe. This is going to be an amazing project.”

With the firing range finished, the second phase of construction will start soon with completion in late 2026. Phase two includes an expansion to phase one’s firing range, a one-mile emergency vehicle operations course, a two-story simunition house, a canine obstacle course training area, a SWAT training area that includes a school bus and fuselage, a drone training area and a training center. That center will house seven classrooms and a virtual training room.

“Currently, there’s not a facility comprised of all these areas in this region,” said Josh Hoeing, Captain for St. Charles City Police Department. “We hope to provide the highest quality of law enforcement training to not only our neighboring municipalities but the entire Midwest region and the country. This center will be a one-stop shop for departments to send their officers.”

Eastern Missouri Police Academy (EMPA) will rehome to CASTLE upon phase two’s completion. The Academy’s board approved the rehoming weeks ago but had to wait for its attorney to sign off on it before they were able to put pen to paper on May 1.

“We really have nice facilities,” said Dr. Thomas Leasor, Executive Director for Eastern Missouri Police Academy. “But as far as the extra type of training—it’s scattered _.”_

EMPA is currently located in Lake St. Louis but attendees have to travel throughout the county for various training functions.

“This will be such a tremendous opportunity to for us to get everything in one location. Our recruits will be around cops every single day. We do a lot of continued education as well but just the facilities and the cooperative group coming together is just such a tremendous opportunity for the academy.”

Leasor noted that training is often brought into question in a courtroom and he commends everyone involved for the CASTLE project.

“It is so profound that these agencies have recognized, and their communities have recognized the demand for training and how that equates to better officers out on the street being able to interact with the public, being able to be trained to use the technology that’s here today.”

# Castle Rock Public Safety Training Facility

Denver

![Image 4](https://bryanconstruction.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/BCI-Flag.svg)

The Castle Rock Public Safety Training Facility is designed to accommodate the training needs of the town’s police and fire departments. The project will consist of a metal building approximately 6,000 square feet, a multipurpose training area, two classrooms, a food prep area, and restrooms. The facility will also include a mezzanine area for mechanical systems. This project also includes site improvements to the parking lot, sidewalks, a detention pond, and required landscaping.

Denver

![Image 4](https://bryanconstruction.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/BCI-Flag.svg)

The Castle Rock Public Safety Training Facility is designed to accommodate the training needs of the town’s police and fire departments. The project will consist of a metal building approximately 6,000 square feet, a multipurpose training area, two classrooms, a food prep area, and restrooms. The facility will also include a mezzanine area for mechanical systems. This project also includes site improvements to the parking lot, sidewalks, a detention pond, and required landscaping.

O’FALLON, Mo. – A new, cutting-edge law enforcement training center in the St. Louis area is inching closer to being completed. We’re talking about the Center for Advanced Skills Training in Law Enforcement (CASTLE) in O’Fallon, Missouri.

The massive, multi-million-dollar facility off of Highway 79 in rural St. Charles County is a partnership between the city of St. Charles and O’Fallon police departments. It will feature a gun range, SWAT and K-9 training and more.

Notably, next month, the facility will open its Emergency Vehicle Operating Cours (EVOC). The 1-mile track could be a game-changer for local law enforcement agencies.

On Wednesday, FOX 2 had the chance to tour the facility, see where the development stands, and learn about why it could be a huge addition to the St. Louis area.

O’FALLON, Mo. – A new, cutting-edge law enforcement training center in the St. Louis area is inching closer to being completed. We’re talking about the Center for Advanced Skills Training in Law Enforcement (CASTLE) in O’Fallon, Missouri.

The massive, multi-million-dollar facility off of Highway 79 in rural St. Charles County is a partnership between the city of St. Charles and O’Fallon police departments. It will feature a gun range, SWAT and K-9 training and more.

Notably, next month, the facility will open its Emergency Vehicle Operating Cours (EVOC). The 1-mile track could be a game-changer for local law enforcement agencies.

On Wednesday, FOX 2 had the chance to tour the facility, see where the development stands, and learn about why it could be a huge addition to the St. Louis area.

**Tulliallan Castle** is a large house in [Kincardine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kincardine-on-Forth "Kincardine-on-Forth"), Fife, Scotland. It is the second structure to have the name, and is a mixture of [Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_architecture "Gothic architecture") and Italian style architecture set amid some 90 acres (36 hectares) of parkland just north of where the [Kincardine Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kincardine_Bridge "Kincardine Bridge") spans the [Firth of Forth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firth_of_Forth "Firth of Forth").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulliallan_Castle#cite_note-:0-1) It has been the home of the [Scottish Police College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Police_College "Scottish Police College") since 1954. On 1 April 2013, Tulliallan Castle became the headquarters of [Police Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Scotland "Police Scotland") (the newly created national police service for Scotland), but in 2014 the service's headquarters temporarily relocated to nearby [Stirling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stirling "Stirling") in the former Central Scotland Police HQ.

## 14th-century castle

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tulliallan_Castle&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: 14th-century castle")]

An earlier structure about 1⁄2 mile (800 metres) northwest, [Old Tulliallan Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Tulliallan_Castle "Old Tulliallan Castle"), was built by 1304, when it was ordered to be strengthened by [Edward I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_I "Edward I") of England, it then passed into the ownership of [William Douglas, 1st Earl of Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Douglas,_1st_Earl_of_Douglas "William Douglas, 1st Earl of Douglas"), and was granted by the Douglases to the Edmonstones, and thence to a junior branch of the [Blackadders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clan_Blackadder "Clan Blackadder"), and finally to the [Bruces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clan_Bruce "Clan Bruce") of Carnock. A [fortified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortified "Fortified") house with a [keep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keep "Keep") and [rib-vaulted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib_vault "Rib vault") ground floor, it was abandoned in the seventeenth century.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulliallan_Castle#cite_note-2)

## 19th-century castle

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tulliallan_Castle&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 19th-century castle")]

The castle was built in 1812–1820 for Admiral [Lord Keith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Elphinstone,_1st_Viscount_Keith "George Elphinstone, 1st Viscount Keith"), one time senior officer of [Lord Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Nelson "Lord Nelson"), paid for with [prize money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prize_money "Prize money"). The labour force said to include French prisoners of war.

During the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War") it was used by the [Polish Armed Forces in the West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Armed_Forces_in_the_West "Polish Armed Forces in the West") as their headquarters in Scotland.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulliallan_Castle#cite_note-:0-1)

Prior to the Second World War there was no central training for police officers in Scotland. After the war it was decided to centralise all police training and Tulliallan was the result. Tulliallan, from the Gaelic _Tulach-Aluin_ ('beautiful knoll') was purchased in 1950 by the then [Scottish Home Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Home_Department "Scottish Home Department") for £9,100. The building was modernised and renovated and the first courses for inspectors and sergeants began in 1954. Over the years the site has been heavily modified to provide accommodation, catering, training, and teaching facilities for the [Scottish Police College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Police_College "Scottish Police College").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulliallan_Castle#cite_note-3)

The building is now used as the administrative head of the Scottish Police College and also serves as the official residence of the Chief Constable of [Police Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Scotland "Police Scotland").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulliallan_Castle#cite_note-4)

The building is sometimes colloquially known as "Castle Grayskull" by serving and retired officers in relation to the castle in the [He Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/He-Man_and_the_Masters_of_the_Universe "He-Man and the Masters of the Universe") fictional series.

**Tulliallan Castle** is a large house in [Kincardine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kincardine-on-Forth "Kincardine-on-Forth"), Fife, Scotland. It is the second structure to have the name, and is a mixture of [Gothic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_architecture "Gothic architecture") and Italian style architecture set amid some 90 acres (36 hectares) of parkland just north of where the [Kincardine Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kincardine_Bridge "Kincardine Bridge") spans the [Firth of Forth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firth_of_Forth "Firth of Forth").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulliallan_Castle#cite_note-:0-1) It has been the home of the [Scottish Police College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Police_College "Scottish Police College") since 1954. On 1 April 2013, Tulliallan Castle became the headquarters of [Police Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Scotland "Police Scotland") (the newly created national police service for Scotland), but in 2014 the service's headquarters temporarily relocated to nearby [Stirling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stirling "Stirling") in the former Central Scotland Police HQ.

## 14th-century castle

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tulliallan_Castle&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: 14th-century castle")]

An earlier structure about 1⁄2 mile (800 metres) northwest, [Old Tulliallan Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Tulliallan_Castle "Old Tulliallan Castle"), was built by 1304, when it was ordered to be strengthened by [Edward I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_I "Edward I") of England, it then passed into the ownership of [William Douglas, 1st Earl of Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Douglas,_1st_Earl_of_Douglas "William Douglas, 1st Earl of Douglas"), and was granted by the Douglases to the Edmonstones, and thence to a junior branch of the [Blackadders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clan_Blackadder "Clan Blackadder"), and finally to the [Bruces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clan_Bruce "Clan Bruce") of Carnock. A [fortified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortified "Fortified") house with a [keep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keep "Keep") and [rib-vaulted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib_vault "Rib vault") ground floor, it was abandoned in the seventeenth century.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulliallan_Castle#cite_note-2)

## 19th-century castle

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tulliallan_Castle&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 19th-century castle")]

The castle was built in 1812–1820 for Admiral [Lord Keith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Elphinstone,_1st_Viscount_Keith "George Elphinstone, 1st Viscount Keith"), one time senior officer of [Lord Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Nelson "Lord Nelson"), paid for with [prize money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prize_money "Prize money"). The labour force said to include French prisoners of war.

During the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War") it was used by the [Polish Armed Forces in the West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Armed_Forces_in_the_West "Polish Armed Forces in the West") as their headquarters in Scotland.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulliallan_Castle#cite_note-:0-1)

Prior to the Second World War there was no central training for police officers in Scotland. After the war it was decided to centralise all police training and Tulliallan was the result. Tulliallan, from the Gaelic _Tulach-Aluin_ ('beautiful knoll') was purchased in 1950 by the then [Scottish Home Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Home_Department "Scottish Home Department") for £9,100. The building was modernised and renovated and the first courses for inspectors and sergeants began in 1954. Over the years the site has been heavily modified to provide accommodation, catering, training, and teaching facilities for the [Scottish Police College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Police_College "Scottish Police College").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulliallan_Castle#cite_note-3)

The building is now used as the administrative head of the Scottish Police College and also serves as the official residence of the Chief Constable of [Police Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_Scotland "Police Scotland").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulliallan_Castle#cite_note-4)

The building is sometimes colloquially known as "Castle Grayskull" by serving and retired officers in relation to the castle in the [He Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/He-Man_and_the_Masters_of_the_Universe "He-Man and the Masters of the Universe") fictional series.
