### Philippines

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: Philippines")]

During the 1980s, the [Philippine National Police Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police_Academy "Philippine National Police Academy") in [Cavite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavite "Cavite") served as a school for selected enlisted personnel and civilians to join as Police/Fire Lieutenants in the defunct [Integrated National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_National_Police "Integrated National Police"). After the merging of the [Philippine Constabulary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Constabulary "Philippine Constabulary") and INP on January 1, 1991, it became the primary officer school for the new [Philippine National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_National_Police "Philippine National Police"), the [Bureau of Fire Protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Fire_Protection "Bureau of Fire Protection") and the [Bureau of Jail Management and Penology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Jail_Management_and_Penology "Bureau of Jail Management and Penology"), all under the [Department of the Interior and Local Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_the_Interior_and_Local_Government "Department of the Interior and Local Government") (DILG).

Philippine National Police Academy graduates are automatically appointed as Inspectors/Lieutenants in the Philippine National Police, Bureau of Fire Protection, or the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology according to their choice of public safety curriculum during their cadetship. This is under the supervision of the DILG and the [Philippine Public Safety College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Public_Safety_College "Philippine Public Safety College").

### Spain

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=51 "Edit section: Spain")]

In Spain, there is a [Ministry of the Interior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_the_Interior_(Spain) "Ministry of the Interior (Spain)")'s [National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Police_Corps "National Police Corps") centralised academy near [Ávila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81vila,_Spain "Ávila, Spain"). The [Guardia Civil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Guard_(Spain) "Civil Guard (Spain)") runs two centralised academies, one for enlisted _guardias_ and [sub-officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-officer "Sub-officer") in [Baeza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baeza,_Spain "Baeza, Spain") and another one for [commanding officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_(armed_forces) "Officer (armed forces)") in two campuses at [Aranjuez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranjuez "Aranjuez") and [El Escorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Lorenzo_de_El_Escorial "San Lorenzo de El Escorial") ([Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_of_Madrid "Community of Madrid")). The autonomous [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalitat_de_Catalunya "Generalitat de Catalunya") and [Basque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basque_Government "Basque Government") police forces —the [Mossos d'Esquadra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mossos_d'Esquadra "Mossos d'Esquadra") and the [Ertzaintza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ertzaintza "Ertzaintza")— also have their own academies in [Mollet del Vallès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollet_del_Vall%C3%A8s "Mollet del Vallès") and [Arcaute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcaute "Arcaute"). No candidates with a criminal record are accepted.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Candidates attend these centralised public academies after passing the police force's [entry examination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_service_entrance_examination "Civil service entrance examination"), this way recruits are already enlisted and will automatically become police officers if they don't fail the course or drop out. Recruits' training is tuition free and the candidates are paid a police cadet's wage as members of the force. Basic training ranges from 9 months for an entry-level officer of the _Policía Nacional_, _Guardia Civil_ or a _mosso_, but realistically takes 18 months to two years including practicums and additional training. Local police forces including [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polic%C3%ADa_Municipal_de_Madrid "Policía Municipal de Madrid")'s or [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu%C3%A0rdia_Urbana_de_Barcelona "Guàrdia Urbana de Barcelona")'s are often trained at these large public academies too. High-rank or highly specialised courses are longer and eventually lead to a college-like degree.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The Spanish police academies must not be confused with the many fee-paying private academies training potential candidates to pass the entry examination beforehand. While these private academies may be helpful, studying at them is not required and potential candidates are able to take the entrance examination without these courses.

### United Arab Emirates

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=57 "Edit section: United Arab Emirates")]

In UAE, the [Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emirate "Emirate") either train their own police force or outsource training to academies of other [Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emirate "Emirate"). There are mainly two academies, one located in [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi") and the other in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai").

#### Abu Dhabi

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=58 "Edit section: Abu Dhabi")]

In the Abu Dhabi Police Academy, the study program includes practical and field training. After successful completion of the program, the student is awarded a bachelor's degree in Law and Policing Sciences.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

An Institute for officer training affiliated with the Police College was established in 1992. In 2002, the system of study in the college was changed to incorporate training theory programs and fieldwork.

The four years of study are divided into two levels of study consisting of eight terms:

##### Basic level – two years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=59 "Edit section: Basic level – two years")]

One year for theoretical study and another for fieldwork.

##### Advanced level – two years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=60 "Edit section: Advanced level – two years")]

These two levels are preceded by an introductory period for the physical and psychological preparation of the students. After successful completion of the study and training programs, the student will be awarded a bachelor's degree in Police Sciences and Criminal Justice.

#### Dubai

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=61 "Edit section: Dubai")]

The Dubai Police Academy was founded in 1987 and was granted autonomy from the police force as long as it retained some affiliation with Dubai Police General Headquarters. It was fully inaugurated in 1989 in the presence of [Sheikh Maktoum Bin Rashid Al Maktoum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Maktoum_Bin_Rashid_Al_Maktoum "Sheikh Maktoum Bin Rashid Al Maktoum"). In 1992, degrees offered by the academy were given university equivalency.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The first class was from 1987 to 1988 and consisted of 51 cadets and 30 full-time students, (some of whom were existing police officers), which graduated in 1991. During the academic year of 1996–1997, students from other Arabic countries such as Yemen and the Palestinian Territories were admitted.

### United Kingdom

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=62 "Edit section: United Kingdom")]

#### England and Wales

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=63 "Edit section: England and Wales")]

All candidates for the 43 police forces for England and Wales must be over the age of 18 1⁄2; of a reasonable standard of physical fitness, with good health and eyesight. Candidates also must hold British citizenship, be a citizen of the Commonwealth with no restrictions on his or her stay within Britain or be a citizen of the Republic of Ireland. There are a number of entry routes, none of which require officers to train at a residential police academy.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-25) From 2007, all training was managed by the now defunct [National Policing Improvement Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Policing_Improvement_Agency "National Policing Improvement Agency") with the [College of Policing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Policing "College of Policing") taking over in 2013.

#### Scotland

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=64 "Edit section: Scotland")]

All new police officers in Scotland attend an initial 11-week training course at the [Scottish Police College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Police_College "Scottish Police College") at Tulliallan Castle.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-26) The college has been operating since 1954 and hosts initial training of new officers as well as a range of courses such as the training of traffic officers and detectives.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-27) Many courses have received accreditation from the [Scottish Qualifications Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Qualifications_Authority "Scottish Qualifications Authority") (SQA) or are credit rated on the [Scottish Credit and Qualifications Framework](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Credit_and_Qualifications_Framework "Scottish Credit and Qualifications Framework") (SCQF). Training ranges from a SCQF Level 7 for the probationer training delivered to new recruits (equivalent to an entry-level higher education course)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-28) to degree level qualifications for more specialised or senior roles such as detective training or courses for senior officers.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-29)

### United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=65 "Edit section: United States")]

Further information: [Police officer certification and licensure in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_officer_certification_and_licensure_in_the_United_States "Police officer certification and licensure in the United States")

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/2014_Wisconsin_State_Patrol_cadet_training_at_Fort_McCoy_%284-20%29.jpg/250px-2014_Wisconsin_State_Patrol_cadet_training_at_Fort_McCoy_%284-20%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2014_Wisconsin_State_Patrol_cadet_training_at_Fort_McCoy_(4-20).jpg)

A [Wisconsin State Patrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin_State_Patrol "Wisconsin State Patrol") cadet driving a cruiser through an Emergency Vehicle Operations Course (EVOC) in 2014

Police academies exist in every state and at the federal level. Each state has an agency that certifies state-specific police academies and their programs. Most states have minimum physical and academic requirements to be completed prior to entry into the academy. Some states may require additional certifications before qualification as a police officer. While some states allow open enrollment in police academies, many require cadets to be hired by a police department in order to attend training. Departments and/or state certification agencies may also require individuals to pass background checks, psychological evaluations, polygraph exams, drug screenings, firearms qualifications and demonstrations of driving skills as prerequisites of employment/certification.

In an analysis of training requirements in several states by _Gawker_ "found Louisiana law enforcement recruits typically attend 360 hours of training, while the national average is approximately 70% higher, at more than 600 hours. Louisiana requires less hours of training for law enforcement than the 1,500 hours needed to become a certified barber, the website said. "Washington, D.C., requires the most police academy training hours in the nation, at 1,120."

Researchers say police are given far more training on use of firearms than on de-escalating provocative situations.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-30)

#### Federal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=66 "Edit section: Federal")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Anchorage_Police_recruits_participating_in_Emergency_Vehicle_Operations_Course_at_Joint_Base_Elmendorf-Richardson.jpg/250px-Anchorage_Police_recruits_participating_in_Emergency_Vehicle_Operations_Course_at_Joint_Base_Elmendorf-Richardson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anchorage_Police_recruits_participating_in_Emergency_Vehicle_Operations_Course_at_Joint_Base_Elmendorf-Richardson.jpg)

[Anchorage Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchorage_Police_Department "Anchorage Police Department")[Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Crown_Victoria_Police_Interceptor "Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptor") used for EVOC training at [Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Base_Elmendorf-Richardson "Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson") in 2018

While some federal law enforcement agencies have their own training requirements and training facilities, 91 federal law enforcement agencies (including the [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") and [United States Marshals Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marshals_Service "United States Marshals Service")),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-31) require agents, officers and prospective agents/officers to attend basic and in-service training at the [Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Law_Enforcement_Training_Centers "Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers") (FLETC). FLETC, which is operated by the [Department of Homeland Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Homeland_Security "United States Department of Homeland Security"), and is headquartered in [Glynco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glynco,_Georgia "Glynco, Georgia"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)") with training sites in [Artesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artesia,_New_Mexico "Artesia, New Mexico"), [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), [Charleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston,_South_Carolina "Charleston, South Carolina"), [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina") and [Cheltenham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham,_Maryland "Cheltenham, Maryland"), [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-32)

#### Connecticut

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=67 "Edit section: Connecticut")]

In Connecticut, police officer recruits receive a certification to enforce the [General Statutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_General_Statutes "Connecticut General Statutes"). Their training is conducted at "The Connecticut Police Academy" located at 285 Preston Avenue, in [Meriden, CT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meriden,_CT "Meriden, CT").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-33) In order to become a certified police officer, a recruit must be a legal United States resident at least 21 years of age, have a high school diploma or equivalent, possess a valid drivers license, and not be convicted of any felonies.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-34) The to be officers then have to attend an 818-hour basic training course that covers various aspects of police work.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-35) This basic training course is certified by [Commission on Accreditation for Law Enforcement Agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Accreditation_for_Law_Enforcement_Agencies "Commission on Accreditation for Law Enforcement Agencies"), (CALEA).

#### Florida

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=68 "Edit section: Florida")]

In Florida, police academies are primarily run by community colleges or state agencies. All law enforcement officers in the state are certified as such by a governing body appointed by the governor called the _Criminal Justice Standards and Training Commission_ under the [Florida Department of Law Enforcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Department_of_Law_Enforcement "Florida Department of Law Enforcement"). All applicants must pass a state examination and be hired by a law enforcement agency within 4 years of graduation to be considered certified.

#### Kentucky

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=69 "Edit section: Kentucky")]

All law enforcement officers in Kentucky, (except as listed below), hired after 1998 are required to complete the minimum screening, physical training and classroom requirements of the Kentucky's _Police Officer Professional Standards (POPS)_ prior to being certified, and acting, as a law enforcement officer.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-auto-36) Larger agencies, such as the [Kentucky State Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_State_Police "Kentucky State Police"), as well as the [Louisville Metro Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Metro_Police "Louisville Metro Police") and the [Lexington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexington,_Kentucky "Lexington, Kentucky") Division of Police, operate their own police academies and may have requirements that exceed the minimum POPS standards. Agencies in Kentucky who do not run their own academies send their prospective officers to a 20-week basic training class at the Kentucky Department of Criminal Justice Training Academy, operated by the [Kentucky Justice and Public Safety Cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Justice_and_Public_Safety_Cabinet "Kentucky Justice and Public Safety Cabinet") and located on the campus of [Eastern Kentucky University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Kentucky_University "Eastern Kentucky University") in [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Kentucky "Richmond, Kentucky").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-auto-36) Exceptions to POPS training and certification are officers hired prior to 1998 and elected law enforcement officers whose duties and requirements are set forth in the [Kentucky Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Constitution "Kentucky Constitution"). These include [sheriffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheriffs_in_the_United_States "Sheriffs in the United States"), [constables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constables_in_the_United_States "Constables in the United States"), [coroners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coroner "Coroner") and [jailers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prison_officer "Prison officer"), (though generally not deputies). Many of these officeholders, however, hold POPS certification from previous employment as law enforcement officers prior to their election and some will receive POPS certification or approved equivalent training before taking office.

#### Maryland

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=70 "Edit section: Maryland")]

In Maryland, the [Maryland Police and Correctional Training Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland_Police_and_Correctional_Training_Commission "Maryland Police and Correctional Training Commission") is the civilian governing body that sets standards for law enforcement personnel within the state. Most major [law enforcement agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_law_enforcement_agencies_in_Maryland "List of law enforcement agencies in Maryland") operate their own academy in which recruits must pass over 550 objectives including, (but not limited to), criminal and traffic law, officer safety techniques, [defensive tactics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-defense "Self-defense"), report writing, a 40-hour block of emergency vehicle operations, a 40-hour block of [First Responder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiopulmonary_Resuscitation "Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation"), and a 40-hour block of weapon training.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-37) Most agencies operate non-resident academies; however, the [Maryland State Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland_State_Police "Maryland State Police") requires recruits to live at the academy and, dependent on their performance level for the week, may leave campus for the weekend.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-38) Many colleges such as the [University of Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Maryland "University of Maryland") and other [community colleges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_colleges "Community colleges") offer police academy instruction as well.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-39)

#### Michigan

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=71 "Edit section: Michigan")]

In Michigan, in order to become law enforcement officers, all applicants have the option to be certified by the _Michigan Commission on Law Enforcement Standards_ or MCOLES. All persons wishing to become police officers in the State of Michigan must be certified through MCOLES. Cadets must pass a physical fitness exam as well as a reading and writing exam. Applicants also cannot have any felonies, weapons violations, or a history of domestic violence posted on their criminal records. Police academies are most often part of [community colleges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_colleges "Community colleges"), city or county police and sheriff departments, or the [Michigan State Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_Police "Michigan State Police").

After the police academy, candidates take the MCOLES test. Upon successful completion, candidates are 'certifiable' and have a period of one year to obtain employment as law enforcement officers, (if not sponsored by an agency). If a candidate is unable to obtain a law enforcement position within that year, and if the candidate wishes to be considered in the future, he/she must attend a two-week re-certification course, which adds a year to the candidate's window of opportunity.

#### New Hampshire

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=72 "Edit section: New Hampshire")]

New Hampshire's PSTC, (Police Standards and Training Council), provides all training and maintains certification standards for every full and part-time law enforcement officer in the state. This includes anyone who has the power of arrest, (except federal officers), under New Hampshire law. The PSTC also provides training and certification for correctional officers employed directly by the State. All recruits must have at least a conditional offer of employment from a law enforcement agency, have a clear background check, pass a medical exam and a physical fitness test. Agencies may add other qualifications such as education, polygraph, and drug exams. The PSTC law enforcement academies require each recruit to qualify with a firearm, demonstrate driving skills, maintaining physical fitness, pass subject matter exams and scenario evaluations as a condition of certification.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-40)

Most agencies in the state use a Field Training Officer program to provide additional training and evaluation of new hires.

#### Texas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=73 "Edit section: Texas")]

The agency which certifies police academies in Texas is the [Texas Commission on Law Enforcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Commission_on_Law_Enforcement "Texas Commission on Law Enforcement") (TCOLE). Many major cities and sheriff's offices also operate their own training academies, while some smaller municipalities cooperate to maintain regional academies. Some community colleges offer police training courses as well. There are three state-level law enforcement academies: the [Texas Department of Public Safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Highway_Patrol "Texas Highway Patrol") which trains state troopers, the [Texas Parks and Wildlife Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Parks_and_Wildlife_Department "Texas Parks and Wildlife Department") who train game wardens, and the [Texas Department of Criminal Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Department_of_Criminal_Justice "Texas Department of Criminal Justice") that trains state [corrections officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrections_Officer "Corrections Officer"). Police academies typically last from 18 to 30 weeks, though there are many variations. All police cadets are required to obtain at least a Basic Peace Officer Proficiency Certification from TCOLE before beginning active duty; some academies also require their cadets to obtain an Intermediate certification before graduating. TCOLE offers certifications for jailers and corrections officers, who must also undergo training prior to being commissioned, (albeit typically much less than police officers).

#### Utah

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=74 "Edit section: Utah")]

The basis of the Utah basic training for police officers is to protect the community and the citizens the officers are serving. They do this by completing basic training, firearms training, curriculum development, canine training, defensive tactics, emergency vehicle operations, and physical fitness training. Training for Utah officers is broken into two separate sections, called blocks. The two blocks are Special Functions and Law Enforcement. In order to be certified in the state of Utah an individual must successfully finish both blocks of training. This training is intended to teach the officers to be as professional and as up to date as possible. Officers are also required to do an additional 40 hours of training annually in order to stay up to date on all current laws and police procedures.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-41)

### Venezuela

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=75 "Edit section: Venezuela")]

[Venezuelan National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuelan_National_Police "Venezuelan National Police") recruits are trained at the [Experimental Security University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_Security_University "Experimental Security University") in [Caracas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caracas "Caracas").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Vietnam

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=76 "Edit section: Vietnam")]

Located in Tu Liem district, [Hanoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanoi "Hanoi"), [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam "Vietnam"), The Vietnam People's Police Academy is one of the leading schools of the [Vietnam People's Public Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_People's_Public_Security "Vietnam People's Public Security"), training officers with university degrees and postgraduate degrees. The People's Police Academy is a training center under the jurisdiction of the [Ministry of Public Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Public_Security_(Vietnam) "Ministry of Public Security (Vietnam)").

In 1968, the People's Police was established within the Department of the Public Security Police (now known as the Academy of the People's Security).

Its primary responsibilities are:

*   Training police officers with university degrees and postgraduate courses;
*   Studying the scientific topics of the National Crime Prevention; Administration of State Security Order, Criminal Law, Works of Justice investigation
*   International Training Cooperation with foreign police academies

In addition to future police officers, it also trains firefighters who serve in the VPPS officer corps.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[**Police academies**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academy "Police academy") worldwide serve as institutions for preparing cadets to uphold law and order, but the standards and training methods vary significantly depending on the academy.

## List of academies by country

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: List of academies by country")]

### Albania

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Albania")]

[Albanian Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albanian_Police "Albanian Police") recruits are trained at the [Security Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_Academy "Security Academy"), located in [Tirana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirana "Tirana").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Australia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Australia")]

In Australia, the [states and mainland territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_Australia "States and territories of Australia") run a centralised academy for the training of law enforcement personnel for agencies within a given state or territory.

The academies ensure that officers meet basic local, state and federal standards. Graduation from an approved academy program is usually required before a new law enforcement officer is placed on [active duty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Active_duty "Active duty").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The [New South Wales Police Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales_Police_College "New South Wales Police College"), [Victoria Police Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Police_Academy "Victoria Police Academy"), [Queensland Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queensland_Police "Queensland Police") Academy, [Tasmania Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmania_Police "Tasmania Police") Academy, [South Australia Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australia_Police "South Australia Police") Academy, [Northern Territory Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Territory_Police "Northern Territory Police") Academy, [Western Australia Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Australia_Police "Western Australia Police") Academy are state police, initial training institutions.

The smaller yet distinguished [Australian Federal Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Federal_Police "Australian Federal Police") Academy located in Barton, Canberra trains AFP recruits.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Azerbaijan

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Azerbaijan")]

In [Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan "Azerbaijan"), the Police Academy was established in 1921 by the People's Internal Affairs Commissariat of the Azerbaijan Republic and it continued to function in Baku until 1936 when the main building of the academy was moved to [Mərdəkan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C9%99rd%C9%99kan "Mərdəkan") (a district outside Baku).

In 1957, it became the Baku Private Secondary Police School of the [Ministry of Internal Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Internal_Affairs_(Soviet_Union) "Ministry of Internal Affairs (Soviet Union)"). The graduates were granted legal diplomas. Initially, education spanned two years. From 1957 to 1961, the school trained personnel for [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(country) "Georgia (country)"), [Dagestan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagestan "Dagestan"), [Kabardino-Balkaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabardino-Balkaria "Kabardino-Balkaria"), [Altai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altai_Republic "Altai Republic"), [Irkutsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irkutsk "Irkutsk"), [Krasnodar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnodar "Krasnodar"), [Kuybyshev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuybyshev,_Novosibirsk_Oblast "Kuybyshev, Novosibirsk Oblast"), [Novosibirsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novosibirsk "Novosibirsk"), [Kemerovo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kemerovo_Oblast "Kemerovo Oblast"), [Saratov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saratov "Saratov"), and other states within the USSR.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-1)

The main purpose of the academy is to educate students regarding the law as well as specialised training for employees of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

All candidates are expected to pass an entry examination composed mostly of fitness requirements. A candidate who does not meet the physical fitness requirements, or fails assessments such as medical or MIA checks are considered to be disqualified from the competition. Applicants must be a citizen of Azerbaijan with no criminal record. The successful candidates graduate after studying for 5 years at the academy.

During the course of study, students of academy are provided with dormitories, uniforms, scholarships, and meals. Men and women are placed in separate dormitories on campus.

After graduation, the candidates are assigned police ranks and they are given positions within the Ministry of Internal Affairs. The academy studies other countries by sending officers to Germany, Austria, England, Spain, Hungary, Poland, Russia, and other countries.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-2)

### Canada

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Canada")]

See also: [RCMP Academy, Depot Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCMP_Academy,_Depot_Division "RCMP Academy, Depot Division")

Cadets of the [Royal Canadian Mounted Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Canadian_Mounted_Police "Royal Canadian Mounted Police") are trained at the [RCMP Academy, Depot Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCMP_Academy,_Depot_Division "RCMP Academy, Depot Division") in [Regina, Saskatchewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regina,_Saskatchewan "Regina, Saskatchewan").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-5) After the recruitment process, successful candidates are scheduled to attend the Academy and begin the Cadet Training Program. Cadets are grouped together in what the force calls "troops". A troop consists of a maximum of 32 men and women who follow their entire 26-week training together. The number of trainees at Depot varies in relation to the demands of the force.

Cadet training is offered in either English only or in an English-French bilingual format, and is 26 weeks long. This is on top of an eight-month-long application process.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-:2-6) Cadets are trained in use of firearms, defensive tactics, police driving, fitness, drill, applied police sciences and more.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-:2-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-:1-7) Cadets receive an allowance during their training of CA$525 per week in exchange for a commitment to becoming an RCMP officer for two years upon hiring. Once training ends, cadets are offered employment with the RCMP and awarded the status of [peace officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_officers "Peace officers").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-:1-7) They must be willing to relocate to anywhere within Canada, even to remote areas of the country.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-:2-6)

Many Canadian municipal and provincial police forces hire police officers who graduated from the RCMP Academy. No one can join the RCMP as a regular member without completing the RCMP Academy's 26-week program. Candidates who are graduates of a police training institution and have served a minimum of two years in a policing role with another Canadian police agency can undergo a five-week learning and orientation program rather than the full 26-week program.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-8)

In addition to training new RCMP regular members, Depot has also been a major continuing-education centre for police in Canada, but is currently tasked primarily with the training of new members and other training is conducted elsewhere. It delivers updated and highly specialized training to experienced RCMP officers and to members of other forces from around the world who want to improve their knowledge.

### Cyprus

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Cyprus")]

The [Cyprus Police Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus_Police_Academy "Cyprus Police Academy"), (Greek: Αστυνομική Ακαδημία Κύπρου), is the main educational institution for law enforcement officers in the [Republic of Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Cyprus "Republic of Cyprus"). Founded in 1990 as the successor to the Police Training School, the CPA is recognised as an institution of higher education by the Cyprus Council for the Recognition of Higher Education Qualifications. The CPA operates under the Ministry of Justice and Public Order as a police unit within the organizational structure of the [Cyprus Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprus_Police "Cyprus Police"). It functions on a permanent basis, both for the education of cadet constables and for the training of all police members, regardless of rank, as part of officers' continuing education. Some legal courses are also conducted for non-police officers.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Czech Republic

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Czech Republic")]

The Police Education and Training Unit (PETU) was established in 2015 and is the leading agency regarding all education and training of the police forces in the Czech Republic.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-9) In the Czech Republic, the Police Academy is a university-level institution, where specialised training for police, public administration, and private security services is provided. Some branches are open to civilians while some are only for police officers and other para-military groups such as firefighters and soldiers. The schools are open to recruits holding advanced educational degrees (bachelor's degree or higher).

Basic training centers for recruits are called "secondary police schools" and every law enforcement officer must advance through one of these centers. In this system, "senior police schools" still exist that have the educational status of "higher learning", where specializations are offered.

Municipal police may have access to several training centers, and some larger cities have their own dedicated campuses. Some municipalities conduct training through privately licensed agencies.

### Estonia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Estonia")]

The Estonian Police was originally established in 1918 and then re-established in 1991 after gaining independence from the Soviet Union. The Estonia Police force consists of three units: Central Criminal Police, the Central Law Enforcement, and the Forensic Service Center. In [Estonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estonia "Estonia"), the Estonian Academy of Security Science is located in [Tallinn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallinn "Tallinn") and consists of four colleges including the Police and Border Guard colleges in [Muraste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muraste "Muraste") and [Paikuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paikuse "Paikuse"). Estonia Police were the first to use Blockchain technology to allow for better policing of the people. Applicants must be in good health, have no criminal background and possess certain traits as evaluated by psychological exams.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-10)

### Finland

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Finland")]

Recruits in the Finnish Police forces receive training at the [Police University College in Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_University_College_(Finland) "Police University College (Finland)"), or POLAMK. It is located in Tampere, Finland and consists of various teaching facilities and related premises, including a vehicle training facility and a training area for live-action, realistic police operations. POLAMK requires its candidates to be Finnish citizens who have completed at least a vocational qualification, upper secondary school studies or the matriculation examination.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Applicants must be in good health, have no criminal background and possess certain traits as evaluated by psychological exams. The [Security Intelligence Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnish_Security_Intelligence_Service "Finnish Security Intelligence Service") performs a basic security background check of all applicants which includes penalties and convictions, arrests for drunkenness, racist attitudes as well as security risks. Applicants must possess, at least, a short-term driving license by the end of the application period.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-11) Basic police training requires three years of study and is considered a bachelor's degree.

After the bachelor's degree and three additional years of experience in the field of internal security, an officer is qualified to apply for Master's studies (2 years, Master's degree). Master's studies focus on management skills and supervisory tasks. The master's degree is a required qualification for command positions such as Chief Inspector or Superintendent.

### France

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: France")]

Entry-level police officers train at National Police Schools ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _Écoles nationales de police, ENP_) located in [Draveil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draveil "Draveil"), [Reims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reims "Reims"), [Roubaix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roubaix "Roubaix") and [Périgueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%C3%A9rigueux "Périgueux") for twelve months. Programs cover criminal law, intervention techniques, and physical training. Internships that allow for operational practice are also available.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-:3-12) Prospective cadets must have a high school diploma.

Cadets training for an intermediate career (between police officer and commissioner) train at the National Superior School for Police Officers ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _École nationale supérieure des officiers de police, ENSOP_) for eighteen months.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-:3-12) Cadets must have a bachelor's degree and undergo twelve months of training at an ENP.

The Central Directorate for Recruitment and Training of the National Police oversees both initial and ongoing training across France. The Higher National Police Academy ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _École nationale supérieure de la police, ENSP_) operates campuses in [Saint-Cyr-au-Mont-d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Cyr-au-Mont-d'Or "Saint-Cyr-au-Mont-d'Or") and [Cannes-Écluse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes-%C3%89cluse "Cannes-Écluse") and is designed for future police commissioners and officers.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-13) It provides education for high-ranking officials, academic training, and preparation for competitive exams and partnerships with universities.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-15) Commissioner cadets are required to have a master's degree and undergo two years of training at an ENSP.

National police training centers offer continuing education in areas including cybercrime and forensic science.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-:3-12)

There are competitive exams for different roles in French police academies.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-:3-12)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Taruna_akpol.jpg/330px-Taruna_akpol.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taruna_akpol.jpg)

Indonesian Police Academy cadets

In [Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia"), the National Police Academy ([Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_language "Indonesian language"): _Akademi Kepolisian, AKPOL_) is the main institute, training center, and school for recruits joining the [Indonesian National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_National_Police "Indonesian National Police") to become professional [officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officers "Officers"). After 4 years in the Police Academy, cadets graduate to the rank of Police Inspector 2nd Class ([Indonesian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_language "Indonesian language"): _Inspektur Polisi Dua_), (equivalent to [Second Lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Lieutenant "Second Lieutenant") in the military). Graduates become first line supervisors with the rank of junior first ranking officers in the Indonesian National Police and can be deployed to different units within the force. The academy is located in [Semarang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semarang "Semarang"), [Central Java](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Java "Central Java") and is part of the International Association of Police Academies.

Cadet ranks in the academy are as shown below:

*   Cadet Enlisted Candidate (_Calon Bhayangkara Taruna_) – Trainee for the first 4 months
*   Cadet Enlisted Second Class (_Bhayangkara Dua Taruna_) – First Year
*   Cadet Enlisted First Class (_Bhayangkara Satu Taruna_) – Second Year
*   Cadet Brigadier Second Class (_Brigadir Dua Taruna_) – Third Year
*   Cadet Brigadier First Class (_Brigadir Satu Taruna_) – Fourth Year
*   Cadet Brigadier (_Brigadir Taruna_) – Graduating year (After this rank, they will graduate and achieve the rank of Police Inspector)

Until 1999, before the [Indonesian National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_National_Police "Indonesian National Police") officially separated from the armed forces (ABRI), the Indonesian Police Academy also stood under the National Armed Forces Academy but now has separated from the Military and is under the auspices of the President of Indonesia, and controlled by the National Police Headquarters (_Mabes Polri_).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Although separated from the service academies, cadets from both institutions maintain cooperative relationships through annual joint exercises. AKPOL's new cadets and fourth class cadets, alongside their armed forces counterparts, have had a joint fourth class cadet training program since 2008, after completing it the police officer cadets spend the remaining four years of study in Semarang.

### Spain

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=51 "Edit section: Spain")]

In Spain, there is a [Ministry of the Interior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_the_Interior_(Spain) "Ministry of the Interior (Spain)")'s [National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Police_Corps "National Police Corps") centralised academy near [Ávila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81vila,_Spain "Ávila, Spain"). The [Guardia Civil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Guard_(Spain) "Civil Guard (Spain)") runs two centralised academies, one for enlisted _guardias_ and [sub-officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-officer "Sub-officer") in [Baeza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baeza,_Spain "Baeza, Spain") and another one for [commanding officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_(armed_forces) "Officer (armed forces)") in two campuses at [Aranjuez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranjuez "Aranjuez") and [El Escorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Lorenzo_de_El_Escorial "San Lorenzo de El Escorial") ([Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_of_Madrid "Community of Madrid")). The autonomous [Catalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalitat_de_Catalunya "Generalitat de Catalunya") and [Basque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basque_Government "Basque Government") police forces —the [Mossos d'Esquadra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mossos_d'Esquadra "Mossos d'Esquadra") and the [Ertzaintza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ertzaintza "Ertzaintza")— also have their own academies in [Mollet del Vallès](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollet_del_Vall%C3%A8s "Mollet del Vallès") and [Arcaute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcaute "Arcaute"). No candidates with a criminal record are accepted.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Candidates attend these centralised public academies after passing the police force's [entry examination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_service_entrance_examination "Civil service entrance examination"), this way recruits are already enlisted and will automatically become police officers if they don't fail the course or drop out. Recruits' training is tuition free and the candidates are paid a police cadet's wage as members of the force. Basic training ranges from 9 months for an entry-level officer of the _Policía Nacional_, _Guardia Civil_ or a _mosso_, but realistically takes 18 months to two years including practicums and additional training. Local police forces including [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polic%C3%ADa_Municipal_de_Madrid "Policía Municipal de Madrid")'s or [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu%C3%A0rdia_Urbana_de_Barcelona "Guàrdia Urbana de Barcelona")'s are often trained at these large public academies too. High-rank or highly specialised courses are longer and eventually lead to a college-like degree.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The Spanish police academies must not be confused with the many fee-paying private academies training potential candidates to pass the entry examination beforehand. While these private academies may be helpful, studying at them is not required and potential candidates are able to take the entrance examination without these courses.
