In Thailand, the [Royal Thai Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Thai_Police "Royal Thai Police") has two levels of police academies:

For police cadets, the Royal Police Cadet Academy is the only training center in the country. Graduates exit with the rank of sub-lieutenant.

Non-commissioned officers graduate from the Police Training Center for Non-Commissioned Officers with the rank of [lance corporal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_corporal "Lance corporal"). The training centers are divided according to operational regions, including the Central Police Training Division for the [Metropolitan Police Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Police_Bureau "Metropolitan Police Bureau").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-24)

### Turkey

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=55 "Edit section: Turkey")]

The [Turkish National Police Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_National_Police_Academy "Turkish National Police Academy") was established in 1937 to recruit police chiefs. In 1938, a police college, was established in [Ankara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankara "Ankara") in order to prepare students for the Police Academy. Today, the police academy recruits police officers in 26 schools located in different parts of Turkey, and police chiefs in one school located in [Ankara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankara "Ankara").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Ukraine

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=56 "Edit section: Ukraine")]

National Police of Ukraine recruits are trained at the [National Academy of Internal Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Academy_of_Internal_Affairs "National Academy of Internal Affairs") in [Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyiv "Kyiv").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### United Arab Emirates

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=57 "Edit section: United Arab Emirates")]

In UAE, the [Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emirate "Emirate") either train their own police force or outsource training to academies of other [Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emirate "Emirate"). There are mainly two academies, one located in [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi") and the other in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai").

#### Abu Dhabi

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=58 "Edit section: Abu Dhabi")]

In the Abu Dhabi Police Academy, the study program includes practical and field training. After successful completion of the program, the student is awarded a bachelor's degree in Law and Policing Sciences.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

An Institute for officer training affiliated with the Police College was established in 1992. In 2002, the system of study in the college was changed to incorporate training theory programs and fieldwork.

The four years of study are divided into two levels of study consisting of eight terms:

##### Basic level – two years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=59 "Edit section: Basic level – two years")]

One year for theoretical study and another for fieldwork.

##### Advanced level – two years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=60 "Edit section: Advanced level – two years")]

These two levels are preceded by an introductory period for the physical and psychological preparation of the students. After successful completion of the study and training programs, the student will be awarded a bachelor's degree in Police Sciences and Criminal Justice.

#### Dubai

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=61 "Edit section: Dubai")]

The Dubai Police Academy was founded in 1987 and was granted autonomy from the police force as long as it retained some affiliation with Dubai Police General Headquarters. It was fully inaugurated in 1989 in the presence of [Sheikh Maktoum Bin Rashid Al Maktoum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Maktoum_Bin_Rashid_Al_Maktoum "Sheikh Maktoum Bin Rashid Al Maktoum"). In 1992, degrees offered by the academy were given university equivalency.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The first class was from 1987 to 1988 and consisted of 51 cadets and 30 full-time students, (some of whom were existing police officers), which graduated in 1991. During the academic year of 1996–1997, students from other Arabic countries such as Yemen and the Palestinian Territories were admitted.

### United Kingdom

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=62 "Edit section: United Kingdom")]

#### England and Wales

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=63 "Edit section: England and Wales")]

All candidates for the 43 police forces for England and Wales must be over the age of 18 1⁄2; of a reasonable standard of physical fitness, with good health and eyesight. Candidates also must hold British citizenship, be a citizen of the Commonwealth with no restrictions on his or her stay within Britain or be a citizen of the Republic of Ireland. There are a number of entry routes, none of which require officers to train at a residential police academy.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-25) From 2007, all training was managed by the now defunct [National Policing Improvement Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Policing_Improvement_Agency "National Policing Improvement Agency") with the [College of Policing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Policing "College of Policing") taking over in 2013.

#### Scotland

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=64 "Edit section: Scotland")]

All new police officers in Scotland attend an initial 11-week training course at the [Scottish Police College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Police_College "Scottish Police College") at Tulliallan Castle.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-26) The college has been operating since 1954 and hosts initial training of new officers as well as a range of courses such as the training of traffic officers and detectives.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-27) Many courses have received accreditation from the [Scottish Qualifications Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Qualifications_Authority "Scottish Qualifications Authority") (SQA) or are credit rated on the [Scottish Credit and Qualifications Framework](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottish_Credit_and_Qualifications_Framework "Scottish Credit and Qualifications Framework") (SCQF). Training ranges from a SCQF Level 7 for the probationer training delivered to new recruits (equivalent to an entry-level higher education course)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-28) to degree level qualifications for more specialised or senior roles such as detective training or courses for senior officers.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-29)

### United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=65 "Edit section: United States")]

Further information: [Police officer certification and licensure in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_officer_certification_and_licensure_in_the_United_States "Police officer certification and licensure in the United States")

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/2014_Wisconsin_State_Patrol_cadet_training_at_Fort_McCoy_%284-20%29.jpg/250px-2014_Wisconsin_State_Patrol_cadet_training_at_Fort_McCoy_%284-20%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2014_Wisconsin_State_Patrol_cadet_training_at_Fort_McCoy_(4-20).jpg)

A [Wisconsin State Patrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin_State_Patrol "Wisconsin State Patrol") cadet driving a cruiser through an Emergency Vehicle Operations Course (EVOC) in 2014

Police academies exist in every state and at the federal level. Each state has an agency that certifies state-specific police academies and their programs. Most states have minimum physical and academic requirements to be completed prior to entry into the academy. Some states may require additional certifications before qualification as a police officer. While some states allow open enrollment in police academies, many require cadets to be hired by a police department in order to attend training. Departments and/or state certification agencies may also require individuals to pass background checks, psychological evaluations, polygraph exams, drug screenings, firearms qualifications and demonstrations of driving skills as prerequisites of employment/certification.

In an analysis of training requirements in several states by _Gawker_ "found Louisiana law enforcement recruits typically attend 360 hours of training, while the national average is approximately 70% higher, at more than 600 hours. Louisiana requires less hours of training for law enforcement than the 1,500 hours needed to become a certified barber, the website said. "Washington, D.C., requires the most police academy training hours in the nation, at 1,120."

Researchers say police are given far more training on use of firearms than on de-escalating provocative situations.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-30)

#### Federal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=66 "Edit section: Federal")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Anchorage_Police_recruits_participating_in_Emergency_Vehicle_Operations_Course_at_Joint_Base_Elmendorf-Richardson.jpg/250px-Anchorage_Police_recruits_participating_in_Emergency_Vehicle_Operations_Course_at_Joint_Base_Elmendorf-Richardson.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anchorage_Police_recruits_participating_in_Emergency_Vehicle_Operations_Course_at_Joint_Base_Elmendorf-Richardson.jpg)

[Anchorage Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchorage_Police_Department "Anchorage Police Department")[Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Crown_Victoria_Police_Interceptor "Ford Crown Victoria Police Interceptor") used for EVOC training at [Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Base_Elmendorf-Richardson "Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson") in 2018

While some federal law enforcement agencies have their own training requirements and training facilities, 91 federal law enforcement agencies (including the [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation") and [United States Marshals Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marshals_Service "United States Marshals Service")),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-31) require agents, officers and prospective agents/officers to attend basic and in-service training at the [Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Law_Enforcement_Training_Centers "Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers") (FLETC). FLETC, which is operated by the [Department of Homeland Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Homeland_Security "United States Department of Homeland Security"), and is headquartered in [Glynco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glynco,_Georgia "Glynco, Georgia"), [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)") with training sites in [Artesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artesia,_New_Mexico "Artesia, New Mexico"), [New Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico "New Mexico"), [Charleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charleston,_South_Carolina "Charleston, South Carolina"), [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina") and [Cheltenham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham,_Maryland "Cheltenham, Maryland"), [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland "Maryland").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-32)

#### Connecticut

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=67 "Edit section: Connecticut")]

In Connecticut, police officer recruits receive a certification to enforce the [General Statutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_General_Statutes "Connecticut General Statutes"). Their training is conducted at "The Connecticut Police Academy" located at 285 Preston Avenue, in [Meriden, CT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meriden,_CT "Meriden, CT").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-33) In order to become a certified police officer, a recruit must be a legal United States resident at least 21 years of age, have a high school diploma or equivalent, possess a valid drivers license, and not be convicted of any felonies.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-34) The to be officers then have to attend an 818-hour basic training course that covers various aspects of police work.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-35) This basic training course is certified by [Commission on Accreditation for Law Enforcement Agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commission_on_Accreditation_for_Law_Enforcement_Agencies "Commission on Accreditation for Law Enforcement Agencies"), (CALEA).

#### Florida

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=68 "Edit section: Florida")]

In Florida, police academies are primarily run by community colleges or state agencies. All law enforcement officers in the state are certified as such by a governing body appointed by the governor called the _Criminal Justice Standards and Training Commission_ under the [Florida Department of Law Enforcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Department_of_Law_Enforcement "Florida Department of Law Enforcement"). All applicants must pass a state examination and be hired by a law enforcement agency within 4 years of graduation to be considered certified.

#### Kentucky

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=69 "Edit section: Kentucky")]

All law enforcement officers in Kentucky, (except as listed below), hired after 1998 are required to complete the minimum screening, physical training and classroom requirements of the Kentucky's _Police Officer Professional Standards (POPS)_ prior to being certified, and acting, as a law enforcement officer.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-auto-36) Larger agencies, such as the [Kentucky State Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_State_Police "Kentucky State Police"), as well as the [Louisville Metro Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisville_Metro_Police "Louisville Metro Police") and the [Lexington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexington,_Kentucky "Lexington, Kentucky") Division of Police, operate their own police academies and may have requirements that exceed the minimum POPS standards. Agencies in Kentucky who do not run their own academies send their prospective officers to a 20-week basic training class at the Kentucky Department of Criminal Justice Training Academy, operated by the [Kentucky Justice and Public Safety Cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Justice_and_Public_Safety_Cabinet "Kentucky Justice and Public Safety Cabinet") and located on the campus of [Eastern Kentucky University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Kentucky_University "Eastern Kentucky University") in [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Kentucky "Richmond, Kentucky").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-auto-36) Exceptions to POPS training and certification are officers hired prior to 1998 and elected law enforcement officers whose duties and requirements are set forth in the [Kentucky Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Constitution "Kentucky Constitution"). These include [sheriffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheriffs_in_the_United_States "Sheriffs in the United States"), [constables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constables_in_the_United_States "Constables in the United States"), [coroners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coroner "Coroner") and [jailers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prison_officer "Prison officer"), (though generally not deputies). Many of these officeholders, however, hold POPS certification from previous employment as law enforcement officers prior to their election and some will receive POPS certification or approved equivalent training before taking office.

#### Maryland

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=70 "Edit section: Maryland")]

In Maryland, the [Maryland Police and Correctional Training Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland_Police_and_Correctional_Training_Commission "Maryland Police and Correctional Training Commission") is the civilian governing body that sets standards for law enforcement personnel within the state. Most major [law enforcement agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_law_enforcement_agencies_in_Maryland "List of law enforcement agencies in Maryland") operate their own academy in which recruits must pass over 550 objectives including, (but not limited to), criminal and traffic law, officer safety techniques, [defensive tactics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-defense "Self-defense"), report writing, a 40-hour block of emergency vehicle operations, a 40-hour block of [First Responder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiopulmonary_Resuscitation "Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation"), and a 40-hour block of weapon training.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-37) Most agencies operate non-resident academies; however, the [Maryland State Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland_State_Police "Maryland State Police") requires recruits to live at the academy and, dependent on their performance level for the week, may leave campus for the weekend.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-38) Many colleges such as the [University of Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Maryland "University of Maryland") and other [community colleges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_colleges "Community colleges") offer police academy instruction as well.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-39)

#### Michigan

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=71 "Edit section: Michigan")]

In Michigan, in order to become law enforcement officers, all applicants have the option to be certified by the _Michigan Commission on Law Enforcement Standards_ or MCOLES. All persons wishing to become police officers in the State of Michigan must be certified through MCOLES. Cadets must pass a physical fitness exam as well as a reading and writing exam. Applicants also cannot have any felonies, weapons violations, or a history of domestic violence posted on their criminal records. Police academies are most often part of [community colleges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_colleges "Community colleges"), city or county police and sheriff departments, or the [Michigan State Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_Police "Michigan State Police").

After the police academy, candidates take the MCOLES test. Upon successful completion, candidates are 'certifiable' and have a period of one year to obtain employment as law enforcement officers, (if not sponsored by an agency). If a candidate is unable to obtain a law enforcement position within that year, and if the candidate wishes to be considered in the future, he/she must attend a two-week re-certification course, which adds a year to the candidate's window of opportunity.

#### New Hampshire

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=72 "Edit section: New Hampshire")]

New Hampshire's PSTC, (Police Standards and Training Council), provides all training and maintains certification standards for every full and part-time law enforcement officer in the state. This includes anyone who has the power of arrest, (except federal officers), under New Hampshire law. The PSTC also provides training and certification for correctional officers employed directly by the State. All recruits must have at least a conditional offer of employment from a law enforcement agency, have a clear background check, pass a medical exam and a physical fitness test. Agencies may add other qualifications such as education, polygraph, and drug exams. The PSTC law enforcement academies require each recruit to qualify with a firearm, demonstrate driving skills, maintaining physical fitness, pass subject matter exams and scenario evaluations as a condition of certification.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-40)

Most agencies in the state use a Field Training Officer program to provide additional training and evaluation of new hires.

#### Texas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=73 "Edit section: Texas")]

The agency which certifies police academies in Texas is the [Texas Commission on Law Enforcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Commission_on_Law_Enforcement "Texas Commission on Law Enforcement") (TCOLE). Many major cities and sheriff's offices also operate their own training academies, while some smaller municipalities cooperate to maintain regional academies. Some community colleges offer police training courses as well. There are three state-level law enforcement academies: the [Texas Department of Public Safety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Highway_Patrol "Texas Highway Patrol") which trains state troopers, the [Texas Parks and Wildlife Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Parks_and_Wildlife_Department "Texas Parks and Wildlife Department") who train game wardens, and the [Texas Department of Criminal Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Department_of_Criminal_Justice "Texas Department of Criminal Justice") that trains state [corrections officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrections_Officer "Corrections Officer"). Police academies typically last from 18 to 30 weeks, though there are many variations. All police cadets are required to obtain at least a Basic Peace Officer Proficiency Certification from TCOLE before beginning active duty; some academies also require their cadets to obtain an Intermediate certification before graduating. TCOLE offers certifications for jailers and corrections officers, who must also undergo training prior to being commissioned, (albeit typically much less than police officers).

#### Utah

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=74 "Edit section: Utah")]

The basis of the Utah basic training for police officers is to protect the community and the citizens the officers are serving. They do this by completing basic training, firearms training, curriculum development, canine training, defensive tactics, emergency vehicle operations, and physical fitness training. Training for Utah officers is broken into two separate sections, called blocks. The two blocks are Special Functions and Law Enforcement. In order to be certified in the state of Utah an individual must successfully finish both blocks of training. This training is intended to teach the officers to be as professional and as up to date as possible. Officers are also required to do an additional 40 hours of training annually in order to stay up to date on all current laws and police procedures.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_academies_by_country#cite_note-41)

### Venezuela

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=75 "Edit section: Venezuela")]

[Venezuelan National Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuelan_National_Police "Venezuelan National Police") recruits are trained at the [Experimental Security University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_Security_University "Experimental Security University") in [Caracas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caracas "Caracas").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Vietnam

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Police_academies_by_country&action=edit&section=76 "Edit section: Vietnam")]

Located in Tu Liem district, [Hanoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanoi "Hanoi"), [Vietnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam "Vietnam"), The Vietnam People's Police Academy is one of the leading schools of the [Vietnam People's Public Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_People's_Public_Security "Vietnam People's Public Security"), training officers with university degrees and postgraduate degrees. The People's Police Academy is a training center under the jurisdiction of the [Ministry of Public Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Public_Security_(Vietnam) "Ministry of Public Security (Vietnam)").

In 1968, the People's Police was established within the Department of the Public Security Police (now known as the Academy of the People's Security).

Its primary responsibilities are:

*   Training police officers with university degrees and postgraduate courses;
*   Studying the scientific topics of the National Crime Prevention; Administration of State Security Order, Criminal Law, Works of Justice investigation
*   International Training Cooperation with foreign police academies

In addition to future police officers, it also trains firefighters who serve in the VPPS officer corps.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
